'''Kotohira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|qid=Q812767|lt=Shinto|1=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|en|Naruto, Tokushima|qid=Q460812|lt=Naruto|1=Naruto, Tokushima}}, Tokushima Prefecture.

== History ==

The shrine was established in {{ill|1601|en|1601|qid=Q6725|lt=1601|1=1601}} (Keichō 6) by Yaeemon Masuda, the lord of {{ill|Muyajō (Hayasaki Castle)|ja|撫養城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muyajō (Hayasaki Castle)|1=Q11498684|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498684}} (Hayasaki Castle). It enshrines a {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=bunrei|1=Bunrei}} (spiritual branch) of the Zōzuzan Konpira Daigongen (now {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|qid=Q94760|lt=Kotohira-gū|1=Kotohira-gū}}) from {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}}. In {{ill|1640|en|1640|qid=Q6901|lt=1640|1=1640}} (Kan'ei 17), the lord of {{ill|Tokushima Domain|en|Tokushima Domain|qid=Q3034557|lt=Tokushima Domain|1=Tokushima Domain}}, {{ill|Hachisuka Tadateru|en|Hachisuka Tadateru|qid=Q3125469|lt=Hachisuka Tadahide|1=Hachisuka Tadateru}}, rebuilt the shrine's structures.

During the early Meiji era's {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu bunri|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535}}, the associated temple {{ill|Hase-dera|en|Hase-dera|qid=Q1457787|lt=Hasedera (Naruto City)|1=Hase-dera}} was abolished, and shrine priests were appointed. In Meiji 3, the enshrined deity was identified as {{ill|Ōmononushi no Mikoto|ja|大物主命|1=Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701}} ([[Konpira Gongen]]), and the shrine's name changed from Konpira Daigongen to its current name. In {{ill|1874|en|1874|qid=Q7761|lt=1874|1=1874}} (Meiji 7), it was designated as a Gōsha.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://awa-jinjacho.jp/shrine/detail.html?id=565|title=Kotohira Shrine|publisher=Tokushima Prefecture Shrine Association|accessdate=2021-03-25}}</ref>

Together with {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City)|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Tokushima City's Seimi-chō and {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Kawauchichō, Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Kawauchichō, Tokushima)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Kotohira shrines|qid=Q11646488}} in Kawauchichō, these three shrines were historically known as "Awa San Konpira." Since the Meiji era, they have been referred to as "Awa San Kotohira."<ref>"History Walks of Tokushima Prefecture" (2009, Yamakawa Shuppansha, p. 105)</ref> The nearby {{ill|Konpiramae Station|en|Konpiramae Station|qid=Q8190757|lt=Konpiramae Station|1=Konpiramae Station}} on the {{ill|Naruto Line|en|Naruto Line|qid=Q861091|lt=Naruto Line|1=Naruto Line}} is named after the shrine.

== Access ==
* By train: Approximately 1 minute on foot from {{ill|Konpiramae Station|en|Konpiramae Station|qid=Q8190757|lt=Konpiramae Station|1=Konpiramae Station}} on the {{ill|Naruto Line|en|Naruto Line|qid=Q861091|lt=JR Naruto Line|1=Naruto Line}}.
* By car: Approximately 15 minutes from the {{ill|Naruto Interchange|ja|鳴門インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naruto Interchange|1=Naruto interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11173861}} on the {{ill|Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|en|Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|qid=Q11590177|lt=Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|1=Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway}} or {{ill|Takamatsu Expressway|en|Takamatsu Expressway|qid=Q7677132|lt=Takamatsu Expressway|1=Takamatsu Expressway}}.

'''Kotohira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|qid=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}} {{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|en|Naruto, Tokushima|qid=Q460812|lt=Naruto City|1=Naruto, Tokushima}} {{ill|Nuyou Town Kizu|ja|撫養町木津|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nuyou Town Kizu|1=Q11498695|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498695}}.

==History==
In {{ill|1601|en|1601|qid=Q6725|lt=1601|1=1601}} ({{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō|1=Keichō}} 6), Masuda Hachiyemon, the lord of {{ill|Nuyou Castle|ja|撫養城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nuyou Castle|1=Q11498684|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498684}} ({{ill|Hayashizaki Castle|ja|林崎城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayashizaki Castle|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 撫養城|1=Q11498684|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498684}}), founded the shrine. He enshrined the Zōtōsan Kotobira Daigongen (now known as {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|qid=Q94760|lt=Kotohira Shrine|1=Kotohira-gū}}) of {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province|1=Sanuki Province}}.
In {{ill|1640|en|1640|qid=Q6901|lt=1640|1=1640}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kan'ei|1=Kan'ei}} 17), Tokushima Domain lord {{ill|Hachisuka Tadateru|en|Hachisuka Tadateru|qid=Q3125469|lt=Hachisuka Tadahide|1=Hachisuka Tadateru}} restored the shrine buildings.

In the early Meiji period ({{ill|Early Meiji|ja|明治初|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Early Meiji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), following the {{ill|Shinbutsu Bunri Edict|ja|神仏分離令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu Bunri Edict|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1970535}}, the hereditary head temple, {{ill|Hase-dera (Naruto City)|ja|長谷寺 (鳴門市)|lt=Hase-dera|lt_ja=長谷寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hase-dera (Naruto City)|1=Chokoku-ji Temple|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11653684}}, was abolished and replaced with Shinto priests. In Meiji 3, the deity was designated as {{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi|1=Ōmononushi}} and the former name of Kotobira Daigongen was changed to the current name. In {{ill|1874|en|1874|qid=Q7761|lt=1874|1=1874}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 7), it was listed as a local shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://awa-jinjacho.jp/shrine/detail.html?id=565|title=金刀比羅神社|publisher=Tokushima Prefectural Shrine Office|accessdate=2021-03-25}}</ref>

Together with the {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrine|lt_ja=金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City)|qq=}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|qid=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}} {{ill|Ikemi Town|ja|勢見町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikemi Town|1=Seimicho|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11400568}} and the {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City Kawachi Town)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市川内町)|lt=Kotohira shrines|lt=Kotohira Shrine|lt_ja=金刀比羅神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City Kawachi Town)|qq=}} in {{ill|Kawachi Town (Tokushima City)|ja|川内町 (徳島市)|lt=Kawachi Town|lt_ja=川内町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Town (Tokushima City)|1=Kawauchichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11477745}}, it has long been known as "Awa San-Kotobira", and since the Meiji period it has been called "Awa San-Kotohira".<ref>"徳島県の歴史散歩" ({{ill|2009|en|2009|qid=Q1996|lt=2009|1=2009}}, {{ill|Yamakawa Shuppansha|ja|山川出版社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamakawa Shuppansha|qq=}}, p105)</ref>
Also, the name of {{ill|Konpiramae Station|en|Konpiramae Station|qid=Q8190757|lt=Kotohira-mae Station|1=Konpiramae Station}} on the {{ill|Naruto Line|en|Naruto Line|qid=Q861091|lt=Naruto Line|1=Naruto Line}} of {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|qid=Q496531|lt=JR|1=Shikoku Railway Company}} is derived from it.

* {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko no Mikoto|ja|猿田彦命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to サルタヒコ}}

==Transportation==
* Approximately a 1-minute walk from {{ill|Konpiramae Station|en|Konpiramae Station|qid=Q8190757|lt=Kotohira-mae Station|1=Konpiramae Station}} on the {{ill|Naruto Line|en|Naruto Line|qid=Q861091|lt=Naruto Line|1=Naruto Line}} of {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|qid=Q496531|lt=JR|1=Shikoku Railway Company}}.
* Approximately a 15-minute drive from the {{ill|Naruto Interchange|ja|鳴門インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naruto Interchange|1=Naruto interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11173861}} of the {{ill|Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|en|Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|qid=Q11590177|lt=Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|1=Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway}} and the {{ill|Takamatsu Expressway|en|Takamatsu Expressway|qid=Q7677132|lt=Takamatsu Expressway|1=Takamatsu Expressway}}.
